subject: Reserved capacity term & phased start — AioScale dedicated options
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reserved capacity — term options & phased start (AioScale)

Hi Elena — great talking earlier. Per our call, attached is v3 of the dedicated pricing proposal with three clean options so procurement can compare quickly. High level: 

- Option A: 12-month reserved commit. Smaller discount, highest per-GPU rate. Good if you want minimal lock-in.
- Option B: 24-month reserved commit. Mid-tier discount; recommended if you expect steady growth.
- Option C: 36-month reserved commit. Best unit economics and one-time onboarding credit.

Key levers described in the PDF: GPU pool sizing bands (S/M/L), guaranteed throughput windows (tokens/sec + concurrency targets), and staged ramp (soft-start) options. For the ramp we propose two choices: a short soft-start (up to 8 weeks) where you pay 50% of committed units for month 1 then ramp to 100%, or a phased ramp spread across 12 weeks with proportional billing.

We also flagged SLA terms (P99 latency targets and crediting mechanism) and invoice milestones (50% on activation, monthly thereafter). If you expect a delayed procurement or infra lead time, we can add a \"start flexibility\" clause to avoid early penalties — effectively shifting the billing start by up to 45 days if mutually agreed.

I've attached the PDF and included a short excerpt of the SLA in a follow-up. Please let me know which term you and procurement prefer and any hard constraints on start date or required throughput so we can provide a redline-friendly contract.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — term options & phased start (AioScale)

Dylan — thanks for the clear options and the PDF. A few clarifying questions from our side before we take this to legal/procurement: 

1) We likely prefer a 12-month to limit long-term exposure, but we need an aggressive phased ramp: our product launch is in Q4 and actual usage is unpredictable for the first 60 days. Can you confirm the 8-week soft-start you mentioned and whether we can get a reduced rate for the first two months while still being on a 12-month term?

2) SLA/credits: procurement needs explicit language for uptime/latency credits and an escalation path if throughput guarantees are missed. Can you send the SLA excerpt?

3) GPU sizing: what happens if our sizing is wrong? Is there a quarterly re-sizing window or ability to swap capacity bands?

4) Discounts and one-time credits: any flexibility for a one-off onboarding credit or an introductory price for month 1?

We'd like to keep pricing simple for procurement. If you can outline a concrete 12-month proposal with a 60-day soft-start and a clear SLA excerpt I can route to our procurement lead and get back quickly.

Best —
Elena Ivanova
Head of Platform, AioScale
elena@aioscale.com

Elena — thanks for the quick review. Answers inline below and I attached the SLA excerpt as promised.

1) Soft-start on 12-month: yes — we can support a 60-day soft-start on a 12-month reserved commit. Proposed billing profile: Month 1: 40% of committed units, Month 2: 70%, Month 3+: 100%. We chose this structure to balance your need for short-term protection with our capacity planning. If you prefer a flat 50%/50% for first 2 months we can discuss but that will affect the effective discount.

2) SLA/credits: see attached redwood_sla_excerpt.pdf. High level — throughput SLOs defined per pool-size, P99 latency targets per model class; if we miss a guaranteed throughput window for more than two rolling weeks you qualify for service credits up to a percentage of monthly reserved fees. There's an escalation ladder (SE -> Support -> Director of Ops) and we can add a named contact for AioScale.

3) GPU sizing: we offer a quarterly resize window with a one-time free resize in the first 3 months. After that, resizes are applied at the next calendar quarter with pro-rated billing adjustments. We can also swap between sizing bands if you commit to a minimum notice period (30 days).

4) Discounts/credits: internally I have room for a one-time onboarding credit (applied against first invoice) and a promotional introductory discount for month 1 if Marissa (sales lead) approves. I'll loop Marissa for sign-off on any concession.

If this sounds workable I can prepare a single-line 12-month term with the 60-day soft-start and the SLA excerpt, then send to DocuSign for signature. Alternatively, I can prepare the 24-month economics as a comparison if you'd like better unit pricing.

Quick summary: 12-month with 60-day soft-start — yes. Quarterly resizes — yes (one free in first 3 months). SLA credits — yes (excerpt attached). Onboarding credit — possible pending Marissa.

Thanks —
Dylan

Attachments: redwood_sla_excerpt.pdf

Marissa — want to sign off on the $25k onboarding credit? If yes I will prepare the 12-month DocuSign with the SLA excerpt and the concession lines called out.
